History of the geographic ranges of lineages, as a stochastic map

Source: R/ranges.R
range_history.Rd

Maps, along the tree of simulate_evolving_metacommunity(), the range of each lineage at each moment, as the combination of areas in which it occupies at least one site: "A", "B", "A+B" and so on, with the areas in the order of their levels. The result is a tree of class simmap, as from trait_mk() or phytools, with the true history, for history_rates(), as_herodotools(), arrival_ages() and region_pool(), and for comparison with ranges reconstructed by models such as DEC (BioGeoBEARS).

Usage

range_history(x, areas, tree = c("reconstructed", "full"))

Arguments

x

An mc_evolving object from simulate_evolving_metacommunity().

areas

Area of each site, in the order of the sites or named by site number; a factor gives the order of the areas in the names of the ranges. Area names may not contain "+".

tree

"reconstructed" (the default) for the tree of extant species, x$tree, or "full" for the tree of all lineages, extinct ones included, x$tree_full.

Value

A tree of class c("simmap", "phylo") with maps (for each edge, the time spent in each range, from its start; a change in the last generation of a tip is kept as a piece without duration, so that the tip has the final range), mapped.edge (edges x ranges, the total time) and root_range, or NULL when the tree is NULL.

Details

The range of a lineage changes at the end of each generation in which it colonises the first site, or loses the last site, of an area. A new lineage starts with the sites it took from its mother. Branches of the tree follow lineages: a branch that continues a mother after a budding is the mother, and the stem of a new lineage is the new lineage. In the reconstructed tree a branch may join several lineages of the full tree (an extinct mother and the descendant that survived), and its map joins their ranges in order. Each tip of the reconstructed tree has the range of the lineage that represents its species (with protracted speciation, not the union of the incipient lineages of the species).

A node has the range of the mother just before the split (the union of the ranges that the mother and the new lineage start with, apart from changes in the same generation), and the tree keeps the range at the root, which no edge shows, as root_range. The stem from the start of the simulation to the first split (root.edge) is not mapped. Nodes of a starting tree, before the simulation, take the union of the ranges at the start of the species below them, and the parts of edges before the start take the range at the start.

See also

history_rates(), as_herodotools(), arrival_ages()

Other simulate metacommunities: as_metacommunity(), colonisation_history(), evolution_control(), genetic_matrices(), growth_rates(), logistic_gradients(), maladaptation(), mc_dynamics(), persistence(), simulate_evolving_metacommunity(), simulate_logistic(), simulate_metacommunity(), simulate_static(), speciation_control()

Examples

set.seed(1)
ls <- landscape_grid(5, disp_scale = 0.5)
areas <- ifelse(ls$coords$x < 2.5, "W", "E")
ancestor <- data.frame(optimum = 50, sigma = 20, r_max = 5, row.names = "sp1")
sim <- simulate_evolving_metacommunity(ls, ancestor, dispersal = 0.01, extirpation = 0.02,
                                       n_steps = 200,
                                       speciation = speciation_control("fission", rate = 0.02))
h <- range_history(sim, areas)
colSums(h$mapped.edge)
#>   W W+E 
#> 132 698
